title.zh: 卷四十一 蜀書十一 霍王向張楊費傳
title.en: Volume 41: Book of Shu 11 - Biographies of Huo, Wang, Xiang, Zhang, Yang, and Fei
title.raw: 卷四十一 蜀書十一 霍王向張楊費傳 Volume 41: Book of Shu 11 - Biographies of Huo, Wang, Xiang, Zhang, Yang, and Fei

sentences.zh: 霍峻字仲邈，南郡枝江人也。

translations.literal: Huo Jun, courtesy name Zhongmiao, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Jun, styled Zhongmiao, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄篤於鄉里合部曲數百人，篤卒，荊州牧劉表令峻攝其眾。

translations.literal: His elder brother Huo Du in the countryside assembled several hundred retainers in a private corps; when Du died, the Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, ordered Jun to take command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: His older brother Huo Du had raised a few hundred local followers; after Du died, Jing governor Liu Biao put Jun in charge of that band.

sentences.zh: 表卒，峻率眾歸先主，先主以峻為中郎將。

translations.literal: When Liu Biao died, Jun led the troops to submit to the First Sovereign, who appointed Jun General of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Biao’s death, Jun brought his men to Liu Bei, who made him a general of the household.

sentences.zh: 先主自葭萌南還襲劉璋，留峻守葭萌城。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign returned south from Jiameng to strike Liu Zhang, leaving Jun to defend Jiameng city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei marched south from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and left Huo Jun to hold the fortress there.

sentences.zh: 張魯遣將楊帛誘峻，求共守城，峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu sent the general Yang Bo to entice Jun, seeking to defend the city together; Jun said, "This petty man's head may be taken, but the city cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu’s officer Yang Bo tried to win him over for a joint defense, but Huo Jun replied, "You may have my head; you will not have this city."

sentences.zh: 」帛乃退去。

translations.literal: Bo thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo withdrew his force.

sentences.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍攻峻，且一年，不能下。

translations.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, attacked, besieged, and assaulted Jun for nearly a year but could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang’s generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun then brought over ten thousand men up the Lang River and besieged the town for the better part of a year without breaking it.

sentences.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，即斬存首。

translations.literal: Jun had only several hundred soldiers in the city; watching for their slackness and gaps, he selected crack troops, sallied out, struck them a great defeat, and beheaded Cun on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Jun had only a few hundred defenders. When he saw an opening, he sent picked troops out in a sortie, routed the besiegers, and took Xiang Cun’s head.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，嘉峻之功，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守、裨將軍。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, praised Jun's merit, thereupon divided Guanghan to make Zitong Commandery, and appointed Jun Administrator of Zitong and Major General.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Bei had secured Shu, he singled out Huo Jun’s exploit, carved Zitong commandery out of Guanghan, and named him its governor with the rank of major general.

sentences.zh: 在官三年，年四十卒，還葬成都。

translations.literal: In office three years, at age forty he died; he was returned for burial at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He served three years in post, died at forty, and was brought home for burial in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先主甚悼惜，乃詔諸葛亮曰：「峻既佳士，加有功於國，欲行爵。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign greatly mourned and pitied him, then issued an edict to Zhuge Liang saying, "Jun is already an excellent gentleman, moreover having merit for the state; I wish to carry out enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei grieved deeply and wrote Zhuge Liang that Huo Jun had been a fine man who had served the realm and deserved a noble rank.

sentences.zh: 」遂親率群僚臨會弔祭，因留宿墓上，當時榮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally led the host of officials to attend the assembly, mourn, and sacrifice, and on that account lodged overnight on the tomb; at the time they deemed it glorious.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the full court to the funeral, stayed the night by the grave, and contemporaries counted it the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 子 霍弋

translations.literal: Son: Huo Yi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Huo Yi

sentences.zh: 子弋，字紹先，行主末年為太子舍人。

translations.literal: The son Yi, courtesy name Shaoxian, in the last years of the Former Sovereign's reign became a gentleman attendant at the heir apparent's palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huo Yi, styled Shaoxian, ended the Former Ruler’s reign as a gentleman attendant at the heir’s residence.

sentences.zh: 後主踐阼，除謁者。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, he was appointed usher.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan took the throne, Yi was made an usher at court.

sentences.zh: 丞相諸葛亮北駐漢中，請為記室，使與子喬共周旋游處。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Zhuge Liang, encamped north at Hanzhong, requested him as secretary, causing him to associate and roam together with Ziqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang, campaigning from Hanzhong, asked him onto his staff as secretary and paired him with Zhuge Qiao for daily companionship.

sentences.zh: 亮卒，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Liang died, he became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuge Liang’s death he rose to gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 後主立太子璿，以弋為中庶子，璿好騎射，出入無度，弋援引古義，盡言規諫，甚得切磋之體。

translations.literal: The Later Sovereign established the heir apparent Xuan and appointed Yi as palace attendant to the heir; Xuan loved riding and archery, going in and out without measure; Yi cited ancient precedents and exhaustively spoke remonstrance, greatly obtaining the manner of mutual refinement.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince Liu Xuan was installed, Huo Yi became his senior attendant. The prince loved the hunt and rode abroad without restraint; Yi quoted classical examples and spoke frankly, in the best tradition of candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 後為參軍庲降屯副貳都督，又轉護軍，統事如前。

translations.literal: Later he became aide-de-camp, deputy commander of the Laixiang encampment, then transferred to protector of the army, directing affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as staff officer and deputy to the Laixiang garrison commander, then as protector of the army, with responsibilities much as before.

sentences.zh: 時永昌郡夷獠恃險不賓，數為寇害，乃以弋領永昌太守，率偏軍討之，遂斬其豪帥，破壞邑落，郡界寧靜。

translations.literal: At the time the Yi and Liao of Yongchang Commandery relied on the precipices and did not submit, repeatedly becoming raiders and harm; thereupon Yi was put in charge as Administrator of Yongchang, led a detached army to attack them, thereupon beheaded their chieftains, destroyed settlements, and the commandery borders were quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal peoples in Yongchang were defying the court from the hills and raiding often, so Yi was named acting governor and led a column against them. He executed their leaders, broke up their villages, and the region grew calm.

sentences.zh: 遷監軍、翊軍將軍，領建寧太守，還統南郡事。

translations.literal: He was promoted army supervisor and General Who Aids the Army, concurrently Administrator of Jianning, then returned to direct Nan Commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to army supervisor and general who aids the army, briefly held Jianning, and then resumed oversight of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 景耀六年，進號安南將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingyao, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: In 263 he was promoted to general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蜀並於魏，弋與巴東領軍襄陽羅憲各保全一方，舉以內附，鹹因仍前任，寵待有加。

translations.literal: That year Shu was annexed by Wei; Yi and the commander of the army at Badong, Luo Xian of Xiangyang, each preserved one region intact, raised them to submit within; all continued their former posts, favor and treatment being increased.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei absorbed Shu. Huo Yi and Luo Xian of Xiangyang, commanding east of Ba, each kept his district intact and surrendered it to Wei; both kept their posts and received heightened favor.

sentences.zh: 〈《汉晋春秋》曰：霍弋闻魏军来，弋欲赴成都，后主以备敌既定，不听。

translations.literal: 〈The Han–Jin chunqiu states: When Huo Yi heard the Wei army had come, Yi wished to hurry to Chengdu; the Later Sovereign, because preparations against the enemy were already settled, did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Han–Jin chunqiu records that when Huo Yi learned Wei was invading, he asked to rush to Chengdu, but the emperor, convinced the defenses were set, refused.

sentences.zh: 及成都不守，弋素服号哭，大临三日。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was not held, Yi in plain garment wailed and cried, greatly mourning three days.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell, he dressed in mourning, wept aloud, and kept vigil for three days.

sentences.zh: 诸将咸劝宜速降，弋曰：“今道路隔塞，未详主之安危，大故去就，不可苟也。

translations.literal: The generals all urged that he should quickly surrender; Yi said, "Now the roads are cut off and blocked; I have not yet learned in detail the Later Sovereign's safety or peril; on a great matter of staying or going, one cannot be careless."
translations.idiomatic: His officers pressed him to yield at once, but Yi said the lines were cut and he still did not know the ruler’s fate; on so grave a choice he would not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 若主上与魏和，见遇以礼，则保境而降，不晚也。

translations.literal: If the sovereign above makes peace with Wei and is met and treated with ritual, then preserving the borders and submitting is not late.
translations.idiomatic: If His Majesty could make peace with Wei and be treated with courtesy, he could still surrender his command intact and not be late.

sentences.zh: 若万一危辱，吾将以死拒之，何论迟速邪！

translations.literal: If by any chance there is peril and humiliation, I will use death to resist it—what talk of slow or fast!
translations.idiomatic: If the worst befell the throne, he would resist to the death, and speed was beside the point.

sentences.zh: ”得后主东迁之问，始率六郡将守上表曰：“臣闻人生於三，事之如一，惟难所在，则致其命。

translations.literal: " Having obtained word of the Later Sovereign's eastward removal, he thereupon led the generals and defenders of six commanderies to submit a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that man's life rests on three, serving them as one; wherever difficulty lies, there one devotes one's life."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the emperor had been moved east, he led the commanders of six commanderies in a memorial: a subject owes his life where duty calls, he said, and would give it where hardship fell.

sentences.zh: 今臣国败主附，守死无所，是以委质，不敢有贰。

translations.literal: Now your servant's state is defeated and the sovereign has submitted; to hold death there is no place; therefore I lay down my pledge and dare not have two hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom had collapsed and his sovereign had yielded; there was no longer a cause worth dying for, so he pledged allegiance and swore he would not serve two masters.

sentences.zh: ”晋文王善之，又拜南中都督，委以本任。

translations.literal: " King Wen of Jin praised it, again appointed him commander of the south center, and entrusted him with his original duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao approved, named him commander-in-chief of the southern interior, and left him in his former post.

sentences.zh: 后遣将兵救援吕兴，平交阯、日南、九真三郡，功封列侯，进号崇赏焉。

translations.literal: Later he was sent leading troops to rescue Lü Xing, pacified the three commanderies of Jiaozhi, Rinan, and Jiuzhen; for merit he was enfeoffed full marquis and his title was advanced to one of lofty reward.
translations.idiomatic: He later led a relief column for Lü Xing, reduced Jiaozhi, Rinan, and Jiuzhen, earned a full marquisate, and received an enhanced title in recognition.

sentences.zh: 弋孙彪，晋越巂太守。

translations.literal: Yi's grandson Biao was Administrator of Yuexi in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Huo Biao became governor of Yuexi under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：罗宪字令则。

translations.literal: The Xiangyang ji states: Luo Xian, courtesy name Lingze.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang ji gives Luo Xian’s style as Lingze.

sentences.zh: 父蒙，避乱於蜀，官至广汉太守。

translations.literal: His father Meng, fleeing disorder, went to Shu, and his office reached Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luo Meng had fled the turmoil into Shu and rose to governor of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 宪少以才学知名，年十三能属文。

translations.literal: Xian in youth was known for talent and learning; at thirteen sui he could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was known for literary talent and could write polished essays at thirteen.

sentences.zh: 后主立太子，为太子舍人，迁庶子、尚书吏部郎，以宣信校尉再使於吴，吴人称美焉。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign established the heir apparent, he became gentleman attendant at the heir's palace, was promoted attendant and gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel of the Masters of Writing, and as Colonel Who Spreads Trust twice was sent on mission to Wu; the men of Wu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince was named, he served as gentleman attendant, then as palace attendant and personnel director at the secretariat, and twice went to Wu as envoy with the rank of colonel who spreads trust, winning praise in the eastern court.

sentences.zh: 时黄皓预政，众多附之，宪独不与同，皓恚，左迁巴东太守。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Hao intervened in government, the multitude attached to him; Xian alone did not join with him; Hao was resentful and demoted him to Administrator of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Huang Hao dominated politics, most officials curried favor, but Luo Xian held aloof; Huang Hao exiled him to the governorship of Badong.

sentences.zh: 时右大将军阎宇都督巴东，为领军，后主拜宪为宇副贰。

translations.literal: At the time the General of the Right Yan Yu supervised Badong as commander-in-chief and was commander of the army; the Later Sovereign appointed Xian as Yu's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: General Yan Yu of the right commanded east of Ba while also leading the central army; the emperor named Luo Xian his second-in-command there.

sentences.zh: 魏之伐蜀，召宇西还，留宇二千人，令宪守永安城。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, Yu was summoned to return west, two thousand of Yu's men were left, and Xian was ordered to defend Yong'an city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded Shu, Yan Yu was recalled westward, leaving two thousand men under Luo Xian to hold Yong’an.

sentences.zh: 寻闻成都败，城中扰动，江边长吏皆弃城走，宪斩称成都乱者一人，百姓乃定。

translations.literal: Soon hearing of Chengdu's defeat, there was disturbance in the city; the senior officials along the river all abandoned the cities and fled; Xian beheaded one who claimed Chengdu was in chaos, and the hundred surnames then settled.
translations.idiomatic: News of Chengdu’s fall threw the town into panic; riverfront magistrates bolted, but Luo Xian executed a man who spread false rumors of riot, and the people calmed down.

sentences.zh: 得后主委质问至，乃帅所统临于都亭三日。

translations.literal: Having received the Later Sovereign's order to submit credentials, he thereupon led those he commanded to attend at the metropolitan pavilion three days.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor’s formal surrender order reached him, he led his troops to the metropolitan pavilion and kept mourning rites for three days.

sentences.zh: 吴闻蜀败，起兵西上，外讬救援，内欲袭宪。

translations.literal: Wu heard Shu was defeated, raised troops westward, outwardly pretending relief, inwardly wishing to strike Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, learning of Shu’s collapse, marched west on the pretext of rescue while intending to seize Luo Xian’s position.

sentences.zh: 宪曰：“本朝倾覆，吴为脣齿，不恤我难而徼其利，背盟违约。

translations.literal: Xian said, "This court has overturned; Wu is lip and teeth; it does not pity our difficulty but seeks its profit, betraying the alliance and violating the covenant."
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian said his dynasty had fallen and Wu, supposedly a close ally, was profiting from Shu’s ruin instead of helping—breaking faith and the treaty.

sentences.zh: 且汉已亡，吴何得久，宁能为吴降虏乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Han is already gone; how can Wu long endure—how could I become a surrendered captive for Wu!
translations.idiomatic: Han was gone, he argued, and Wu could not last; he would never surrender to become Wu’s prisoner.

sentences.zh: ”保城缮甲，告誓将士，厉以节义，莫不用命。

translations.literal: " He protected the city, repaired armor, announced oath to generals and soldiers, exhorted them with integrity and righteousness; none did not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened the walls and arms, rallied his officers on their honor, and every man obeyed.

sentences.zh: 吴闻锺、邓败，百城无主，有兼蜀之志，而巴东固守，兵不得过，使步协率众而西。

translations.literal: Wu heard Zhong and Deng were defeated, a hundred cities had no master, and had the intention to annex Shu, but Badong firmly held and troops could not pass, so they sent Bu Xie to lead the host westward.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui and Deng Ai fell, Wu saw a chance to swallow Shu, but Luo Xian’s grip on Badong blocked the route, so Wu sent Bu Xie west with an army.

sentences.zh: 宪临江拒射，不能御，遣参军杨宗突围北出，告急安东将军陈骞，又送文武印绶、任子诣晋王。

translations.literal: Xian along the river resisted with archery, could not withstand it, sent aide-de-camp Yang Zong to break the encirclement northward, report emergency to General Who Pacifies the East Chen Qian, and also sent civil and military seals and cords and hostage sons to the King of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian’s bowmen along the river could not hold the line; he sent Yang Zong through the encirclement to Chen Qian and forwarded seals and hostages to the king of Jin.

sentences.zh: 协攻城，宪出与战，大破其军。

translations.literal: Xie attacked the city; Xian went out and fought with him, greatly smashing his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Bu Xie assaulted the walls, Luo Xian sallied out and shattered his force.

sentences.zh: 孙休怒，复遣陆抗等帅众三万人增宪之围。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu was angry and again sent Lu Kang and others to lead thirty thousand men to increase the siege of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, furious, sent Lu Kang with thirty thousand more men to tighten the siege.

sentences.zh: 被攻凡六月日而救援不到，城中疾病大半。

translations.literal: Being attacked in all six months and relief not arriving, in the city sickness was more than half.
translations.idiomatic: The siege ran half a year without relief, and disease laid low most of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 或说宪奔走之计，宪曰：“夫为人主，百姓所仰，危不能安，急而弃之，君子不为也，毕命於此矣。

translations.literal: Someone urged Xian on a plan of flight; Xian said, "Now as a people's lord, what the hundred surnames look up to, in peril unable to secure, in urgency abandoning them—a gentleman does not do this; I complete my life here."
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged retreat, he replied that a leader owed the people steadiness in danger; to bolt in a crisis was unworthy of a gentleman, and he would see the defense through here.

sentences.zh: ”陈骞言於晋王，遣荆州刺史胡烈救宪，抗等引退。

translations.literal: " Chen Qian spoke to the King of Jin, who sent the Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie to rescue Xian; Kang and others drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian persuaded the king of Jin to send Hu Lie from Jingzhou; Lu Kang then lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 晋王即委前任，拜宪凌江将军，封万年亭侯。

translations.literal: The King of Jin thereupon entrusted his former post, appointed Xian General Who Crosses the River, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wannian village.
translations.idiomatic: The king confirmed him in office, named him general who crosses the river, and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 会武陵四县举众叛吴，以宪为武陵太守巴东监军。

translations.literal: It happened that four counties of Wuling raised hosts and rebelled against Wu; Xian was made Administrator of Wuling and army supervisor of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: When four Wuling counties rose against Wu, he was appointed governor of Wuling and army supervisor for east of Ba.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年改封西鄂县侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi his fief was changed to Marquis of Xi'e county.
translations.idiomatic: In 265 his title was transferred to marquis of Xi'e county.

sentences.zh: 宪遣妻子居洛阳，武帝以子袭为给事中。

translations.literal: Xian sent wife and children to dwell at Luoyang; Emperor Wu appointed his son Xi as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his family to Luoyang, and Emperor Wu of Jin gave his son Luo Xi a post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，入朝，进位冠军将军、假节。

translations.literal: In the third year, winter, he entered court, was advanced in rank to General Who Vanquishes Champions, and granted credentials.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 267 he attended court and was promoted to general who vanquishes champions with ceremonial credentials.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，从帝宴于华林园，诏问蜀大臣子弟，后问先辈宜时叙用者，宪荐蜀郡常忌、杜轸、寿良、巴西陈寿、南郡高轨、南阳吕雅、许国、江夏费恭、琅邪诸葛京、汝南陈裕，即皆叙用，咸显於世。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, third month, he followed the Emperor feasting in Hualin Garden; an edict asked about sons and younger brothers of Shu great ministers, afterward asking which elders of former times should be employed in due season; Xian recommended Chang Ji of Shu commandery, Du Zhen, Shou Liang, Chen Shou of Baxi, Gao Gui of Nan commandery, Lü Ya, Xu Guo, Fei Gong of Jiangxia, Zhuge Jing of Langye, Chen Yu of Runan; all were at once employed in order, all illustrious in the age.
translations.idiomatic: At a spring banquet in Hualin Park in 268, the emperor asked which Shu officials’ sons and which veteran worthies should be employed; Luo Xian nominated Chang Ji, Du Zhen, Shou Liang, Chen Shou, Gao Gui, Lü Ya, Xu Guo, Fei Gong, Zhuge Jing, and Chen Yu, and every name he offered was soon in office and well known.

sentences.zh: 宪还，袭取吴之巫城，因上伐吴之策。

translations.literal: Xian returned, raided and took Wu's Wucheng, and thereupon submitted a plan to attack Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When he came back he struck east, captured the Wu outpost at Wucheng, and followed with a memorial urging a campaign against Wu.

sentences.zh: 宪方亮严正，待士不倦，轻财好施，不治产业。

translations.literal: Xian was square, bright, stern, and correct, treating gentlemen without weariness, lightening wealth and loving generosity, not managing estates.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and austere, tireless with his men, generous with his purse, and uninterested in amassing property.

sentences.zh: 六年薨，赠安南将军，谥曰烈侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; posthumously he was awarded General Who Pacifies the South, posthumous name Marquis Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 270 and was posthumously named general who pacifies the south with the epithet “martial marquis.”

sentences.zh: 子袭，以凌江将军领部曲，早卒，追赠广汉太守。

translations.literal: The son Xi, as General Who Crosses the River leading retainers, died early; posthumously he was awarded Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luo Xi, general who crosses the river leading family troops, died young and was honored posthumously as governor of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 袭子徽，顺阳内史，永嘉五年为王如所杀。

translations.literal: Xi's son Hui was interior secretary of Shunyang; in the fifth year of Yongjia he was killed by Wang Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xi’s son Hui served as interior secretary of Shunyang and was killed by the rebel Wang Ru in 311.

sentences.zh: 此作“献”，名与本传不同，未详孰是也。〉

translations.literal: Here the name is written with an alternate graph for xian, not matching this biography; which form is correct is unclear.〉
translations.idiomatic: The excerpt uses a different character for the name than our main text; it is unclear which spelling is right.〉

sentences.zh: 王連字文儀，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lian, courtesy name Wenyi, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lian, styled Wenyi, was a native of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時入蜀為梓潼令。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he entered Shu and became magistrate of Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he entered Shu and served as magistrate of Zitong.

sentences.zh: 先主起事葭萌，進軍來南，連閉城不降，先主義之，不強逼也。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign raised troops at Jiameng and advanced the army coming south; Lian closed the city and would not submit; the First Sovereign deemed him righteous and did not force him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei rose at Jiameng and marched south, Wang Lian shut the gates and refused to yield; Liu Bei respected his stand and did not press the siege.

sentences.zh: 及成都既平，以連為什邡令，轉在廣都，所居有績。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was already pacified, Lian was appointed magistrate of Shifang, transferred to Guangdu, and where he dwelt there was achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell he was named magistrate of Shifang, then moved to Guangdu, and in each post he left a strong record.

sentences.zh: 遷司鹽校尉，較鹽鐵之利，利入甚多，有裨國用，於是簡取良才以為官屬，若呂乂、杜祺、劉干，終皆至大官，自連所拔也。

translations.literal: He was promoted Colonel Director of Salt, compared the profits of salt and iron, profit income was very great, benefiting state use; thereupon he selected and took fine talent to be office subordinates, such as Lü Yi, Du Qi, Liu Gan; in the end all reached high office, from Lian's raising them.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to colonel director of salt, where he tightened the salt-and-iron accounts and greatly increased revenue for the treasury. He recruited able men—Lü Yi, Du Qi, and Liu Gan among them—who all rose to high rank on his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 遷蜀郡太守、興業將軍，領鹽府如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted Administrator of Shu commandery and General Who Establishes Enterprise, concurrently directing the salt office as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Shu and general who establishes enterprise while continuing to head the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 建興元年，拜屯騎校尉，領丞相長史，封平陽亭侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was appointed Colonel of Garrisoned Cavalry, concurrently chief clerk to the chancellor, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang village.
translations.idiomatic: In 223 he became colonel of garrisoned cavalry, chief clerk to the chancellor, and village marquis of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 時南方諸郡不賓，諸葛亮將自征之，連諫以為「此不毛之地，疫癘之鄉，不宜以一國之望，冒險而行」。

translations.literal: At the time the southern commanderies did not submit; Zhuge Liang was about to personally campaign against them; Lian remonstrated deeming that "this is barren land, a region of pestilence; it is not fitting that the hope of the whole state risk danger in going."
translations.idiomatic: When the southern tribes rebelled, Zhuge Liang prepared to lead the expedition himself; Wang Lian urged against it, calling the south barren, fever-ridden country unfit for the kingdom’s chief minister to hazard in person.

sentences.zh: 亮慮諸將才不及己，意欲必往而連言輒懇至，故停留者久之。

translations.literal: Liang worried the generals' talent did not match his own, his intention wished certainly to go, but Lian's words were always earnest and thorough, therefore he halted and remained long.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang doubted any general could replace him, yet Wang Lian’s pleas were so earnest that the campaign was delayed for a long while.

sentences.zh: 會連卒。

translations.literal: It happened that Lian died.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Lian died.

sentences.zh: 子山嗣，官至江陽太守。

translations.literal: The son Shan succeeded; his office reached Administrator of Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Shan inherited the title and rose to governor of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 向朗字巨達，襄陽宜城人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Lang, courtesy name Juda, was a man of Yicheng in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang, styled Juda, came from Yicheng in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《襄阳记》曰：朗少师事司马德操，与徐元直、韩德高、庞士元皆亲善。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Xiangyang ji states: In youth Lang studied under Sima Decao and with Xu Yuanzhi, Han Degao, and Pang Shiyuan was all intimate and friendly.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang ji notes that in his youth he studied under Sima Hui and was close to Xu Shu, Han Song, and Pang Tong.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表以為臨沮長。

translations.literal: The Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, appointed him magistrate of Linju.
translations.idiomatic: Jing governor Liu Biao made him magistrate of Linju.

sentences.zh: 表卒，歸先主。

translations.literal: When Biao died, he returned to the First Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Biao died he went over to Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 先主定江南，使朗督秭歸、夷道、巫

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled south of the Yangzi, sending Lang to supervise Zigui, Yidao, and Wu
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Bei had secured the south bank of the Yangzi, he put Xiang Lang in charge of Zigui, Yidao, and Wu

translations.literal: (mountain)
translations.idiomatic: (mountain)

sentences.zh: 、夷陵四縣軍民事。

translations.literal: , and Yiling four counties' military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: , and Yiling—four counties’ civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 蜀既平，以朗為巴西太守，頃之轉任，又徙房陵。

translations.literal: When Shu was already pacified, Lang was appointed Administrator of Baxi; shortly he was transferred in duty, again moved to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he became governor of Baxi, was shifted to other posts, and was later transferred to Fangling.

sentences.zh: 后主践阼，为步兵校尉，代王连领丞相长史。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign ascended the throne, he became Colonel of Foot Soldiers, replacing Wang Lian to lead chief clerk to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shan took the throne, Xiang Lang became colonel of foot soldiers and succeeded Wang Lian as chief clerk to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 丞相亮南征，朗留统后事。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Liang campaigned south, Lang remained to direct rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhuge Liang's southern expedition he stayed behind to manage the capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，隨亮漢中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he followed Liang to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 227 he followed Zhuge Liang to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 朗素與馬謖善，謖逃亡，朗知情不舉，亮恨之，免官還成都。

translations.literal: Lang had always been on good terms with Ma Su; when Su fled, Lang knew the situation but did not report; Liang resented it, dismissed him from office and returned him to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Ma Su; when Ma fled after his defeat, Xiang Lang knew but said nothing. Zhuge Liang, furious, stripped him of rank and sent him back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 數年，為光祿勳，亮卒後徒左將軍，追論舊功，封顯明亭侯，位特進。

translations.literal: After several years he became superintendent of the imperial household; after Liang died he was transferred general of the left, old merit was reviewed in retrospect, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xianming village, rank specially advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he became superintendent of the imperial household; after Zhuge Liang's death he was promoted to general of the left, enfeoffed as village marquis of Xianming for past service, and given the specially advanced rank.

sentences.zh: 初，朗少時雖涉獵文學，然不治素檢，以吏能稱。

translations.literal: At first, in Lang's youth although he broadly read letters and learning, yet he did not regulate plain conduct, and was praised for clerkly ability.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had read widely but cared little for personal restraint and was known chiefly as a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 自去長史，優遊無事垂三十年，

translations.literal: From leaving chief clerk, leisurely roaming without affairs for nearly thirty years,
translations.idiomatic: After he left the chief clerkship he lived at ease for almost thirty years,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：朗坐马谡免长史，则建兴六年中也。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi examines: Lang because of Ma Su sat and was dismissed from chief clerk, then it was in the sixth year of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Xiang Lang lost the chief clerk's post over Ma Su in 228,

sentences.zh: 朗至延熙十年卒，整二十年耳，此云“三十”，字之误也。〉

translations.literal: Lang reached the tenth year of Yanxi and died, a full twenty years only; this saying "thirty" is a character error.〉
translations.idiomatic: and died in 247—only twenty years later—so the text's "thirty" is a scribal error.〉

sentences.zh: 乃更潛心典籍，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he further immersed his mind in canons and records, tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: He then devoted himself to the classics with tireless energy.

sentences.zh: 年逾八十，猶手自校書，刊定謬誤，積聚篇卷，於時最多。

translations.literal: Past eighty sui, still personally by hand collated books, corrected errors, accumulated fascicles and rolls; at the time the most.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty he still collated texts by hand, emended errors, and amassed the largest private library of his day.

sentences.zh: 開門接賓，誘納後進，但講論古義，不干時事，以是見稱。

translations.literal: Opening the gate to receive guests, enticing and admitting later comers, only lecturing and discussing ancient meanings, not interfering in current affairs; on this account he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed guests, encouraged younger scholars, discoursed only on antiquity, and steered clear of politics, for which people admired him.

sentences.zh: 上自執政，下及童冠，皆敬重焉。

translations.literal: Above from those holding power, below reaching youths in caps, all respected and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: From high ministers down to schoolboys, everyone held him in respect.

sentences.zh: 延熙十年卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yanxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 247.

sentences.zh: 〈襄阳记曰：朗遗言戒子曰：“传称师克在和不在众，此言天地和则万物生，君臣和则国家平，九族和则动得所求，静得所安，是以圣人守和，以存以亡也。

translations.literal: 〈The Xiangyang ji states: Lang's dying words admonished his sons saying, "The tradition says the army conquers in harmony, not in multitude; this speaks of heaven and earth in harmony then the myriad things are born, ruler and minister in harmony then the state is peaceful, nine clans in harmony then in motion obtaining what is sought, in rest obtaining what is secure; therefore the sage guards harmony, thereby to preserve and thereby to perish."
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang ji records his deathbed advice to his sons: the classics say victory lies in harmony, not numbers; when heaven and earth, ruler and minister, and kin are at peace, life thrives and the state is calm, which is why sages cling to harmony for survival or ruin.

sentences.zh: 吾，楚国之小子耳，而早丧所天，为二兄所诱养，使其性行不随禄利以堕。

translations.literal: I am but a petty fellow of the state of Chu, yet early lost what heaven gave; was enticed and raised by two elder brothers, causing my nature and conduct not to follow salary and profit so as to fall.
translations.idiomatic: He called himself a humble man of Chu who had lost his father young and been reared by two older brothers so that his character never sank into greed for rank and pay.

sentences.zh: 今但贫耳；

translations.literal: Now I am only poor;
translations.idiomatic: Today I am simply poor;

sentences.zh: 贫非人患，惟和为贵，汝其勉之！

translations.literal: Poverty is not man's calamity; only harmony is precious—do you exert yourself therein!
translations.idiomatic: Want is not the worst affliction; harmony is what counts—strive for that!
Thus ends the quotation.〉

sentences.zh: 子條嗣，景耀中為御史中丞。

translations.literal: The son Tiao succeeded; in the Jingyao period he became imperial secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang Tiao inherited the line and under the Jingyao reign served as imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 〈襄阳记曰：条字文豹，亦博学多识，入晋为江阳太守、南中军司马。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Xiangyang ji states: Tiao's courtesy name Wenbao; he too was broadly learned and knew much; entering Jin he became Administrator of Jiangyang and army major of the south center.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Xiangyang ji adds that Tiao, styled Wenbao, was learned and well read; under the Jin he governed Jiangyang and served as army major in the southern interior.〉

sentences.zh: 侄 向寵

translations.literal: Nephew: Xiang Chong
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Xiang Chong

sentences.zh: 張裔字君嗣，蜀郡成都人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Jinsi, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, styled Jinsi, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 治《公羊春秋》，博涉《史》、《漢》。

translations.literal: He studied the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and broadly perused the Records and the Han.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Gongyang tradition of the Spring and Autumn and read widely in the Records of the Historian and the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 汝南許文休入蜀，謂裔干裡敏捷，是中夏鐘元常之倫也。

translations.literal: When Xu Wenxiu of Runan entered Shu, he said Yi was keen and nimble in affairs, of the same class as Zhong Yuanchang of the central plain.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jing of Runan, on entering Shu, pronounced Zhang Yi as quick and capable in office as Zhong Yao of the central plain.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時，舉孝廉，為魚復長，還州署從事，領帳下司馬。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was recommended filial and incorrupt, became magistrate of Yufu, returned to the province to hold staff aide, and led marshal under the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he was nominated filial and incorrupt, served as magistrate of Yufu, then came back to headquarters as an aide and marshal of the guard.

sentences.zh: 張飛自荊州由墊江入，璋授裔兵，拒張飛於德陽陌下，軍敗，還成都。

translations.literal: Zhang Fei from Jing Province entered by Dianjiang; Zhang gave Yi troops to resist Zhang Fei below the roads of Deyang; the army was defeated; he returned to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Fei marched in from Jingzhou via Dianjiang, Liu Zhang gave Zhang Yi troops to block him on the Deyang plain; Yi was beaten and withdrew to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 為璋奉使詣先主，先主許以禮其君而安其人也，裔還，城門乃開。

translations.literal: For Zhang he carried mission to the First Sovereign; the First Sovereign promised to treat his lord with ritual and secure his people; Yi returned, and then the city gates were opened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi went to Liu Bei as Liu Zhang’s envoy; Liu Bei pledged to honor Zhang’s lord and spare the people, whereupon Yi returned and the gates were opened.

sentences.zh: 先主以裔巴郡太守，還為司金中郎將，典作農戰之器。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign appointed Yi Administrator of Ba commandery, then returned him to be General of the Household for Metals, directing the making of agricultural and military implements.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei first made him governor of Ba, then recalled him as general of the household for metals to oversee farm tools and weapons.

sentences.zh: 先是，益州郡殺太守正昂，耆率雍闓恩信著於南土，使命周旋，遠通孫權。

translations.literal: Before this, Yizhou commandery killed the Administrator Zheng Ang; the elder leader Yong Kai's grace and trust were renowned in the southern land; envoys went back and forth, far communicating with Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yizhou commandery had slain Governor Zheng Ang; the chieftain Yong Kai, influential in the south, sent envoys and opened contact with Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 乃以裔為益州太守，逕往至郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was made Administrator of Yizhou, going straight to arrive at the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was therefore named governor of Yizhou and went straight to his post.

sentences.zh: 闓遂趑趄不賓，假鬼教曰：「張府君如瓠壺，外雖澤而內實粗，不足殺，令縛與吳。

translations.literal: Kai thereupon hesitated and did not submit, feigning ghost instruction saying, "Administrator Zhang is like a gourd vessel: outside although glossy yet inside truly coarse; not worth killing—order bind him and give to Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Yong Kai stalled and refused allegiance, forged a spirit oracle, and said Governor Zhang was like a lacquered gourd—shiny outside but worthless inside—and should be bound and handed over to Wu.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂送裔於權。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sent Yi to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent Zhang Yi as a captive to Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 會先主薨，諸葛亮遣鄧芝使吳，亮令芝言次可從權請裔。

translations.literal: It happened the First Sovereign died; Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi on mission to Wu; Liang ordered Zhi in the course of conversation to be able to request Yi from Quan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei died, Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi to Wu and told him to seize an opening to ask Sun Quan for Zhang Yi’s release.

sentences.zh: 裔自至吳數年，流徒伏匿，權未之知也，故許芝遣裔。

translations.literal: From the time Yi arrived in Wu several years, drifting, hiding, Quan did not know of him, therefore permitted Zhi to send Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi had spent years in Wu in obscurity, and Sun Quan had lost track of him, so he agreed to let Deng Zhi take him back.

sentences.zh: 裔臨發，權乃引見。

translations.literal: When Yi was about to depart, Quan thereupon summoned audience.
translations.idiomatic: Just before Zhang Yi sailed, Sun Quan finally received him in audience.

sentences.zh: 問裔曰：「蜀卓氏寡女，亡奔司馬相如，貴土風俗何以乃爾乎？

translations.literal: He asked Yi saying, "Shu's Zhuo clan's widowed daughter fled to join Sima Xiangru—how is it that your land's customs are thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked how Shu custom could allow a Zhuo widow to run off with Sima Xiangru as legend told.

sentences.zh: 」裔對曰：「愚以為卓氏之寡女，猶賢於買臣之妻。

translations.literal: " Yi replied saying, "Your foolish servant thinks the Zhuo clan's widowed daughter was still worthier than Mai Chen's wife."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi answered that, in his view, the Zhuo widow had shown more sense than the wife of Zhu Maichen.

sentences.zh: 」權又謂裔曰：「君還，必用事西朝，終不作田父子閭裡也，將何以報我？

translations.literal: " Quan further said to Yi, "When you return, you will surely hold office in the western court; in the end you will not be a farmer father and son in the lanes—how will you repay me?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan added that once Zhang Yi was back in Shu he would surely rise high and would not stay a rustic—how would he repay Wu’s kindness?

sentences.zh: 」裔對曰：「裔負罪而歸，將委命有司。

translations.literal: " Yi replied saying, "Yi bearing guilt returns, will entrust his life to the authorities."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi said he was returning under a cloud and would leave his fate to the law.

sentences.zh: 若蒙僥倖得全首領，五十八已前父母之年也，自此已後大王之賜也。

translations.literal: If by good fortune permitted to preserve head and neck, fifty-eight and before is parents' years; from this after is the Great King's gift.
translations.idiomatic: If he escaped execution, fifty-eight would be a full span like his parents’ lives; anything beyond that he would owe to the king of Wu’s mercy.

sentences.zh: 」權言笑歡悅，有器裔之色。

translations.literal: " Quan spoke and laughed, pleased and delighted, having the look of one who esteems Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan laughed and showed open regard for him.

sentences.zh: 裔出閣，深悔不能陽愚，即便就船，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Yi left the pavilion, deeply regretted being unable to feign stupidity, then immediately boarded ship, doubling roads and combining marches.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the hall, Zhang Yi regretted he had not played the fool; he went straight to the boat and raced homeward at double speed.

sentences.zh: 權果追之，裔已入永安界數十里，追者不能及。

translations.literal: Quan indeed pursued him; Yi had already entered Yong'an border several tens of li; pursuers could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan did send pursuers, but Zhang Yi was already dozens of li inside Yong’an and they could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 既至蜀，丞相亮以為參軍，署府事，又領益州治中從事。

translations.literal: Having reached Shu, Chancellor Liang made him aide-de-camp, assigned bureau affairs, and also led Yizhou administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Shu, Zhuge Liang made him an army adviser with charge of headquarters business and added the post of administrative aide for Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 亮出駐漢中，裔以射聲校尉領留府長史，常稱曰：「公賞不遺遠，罰不阿近，爵不可以無功取，刑不可以貴勢免，此賢愚之所以僉忘其身者也。

translations.literal: When Liang went out and encamped at Hanzhong, Yi as Colonel of Archers Who Sound the Charge led chief clerk of the rear headquarters, often declaring saying, "The Duke's rewards do not omit the distant, punishments do not partial the near; noble rank may not be taken without merit, punishment may not be escaped by noble power—this is why worthy and foolish alike forget their persons."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang moved to Hanzhong, Zhang Yi stayed behind as colonel of the archers’ guard and chief clerk of the rear headquarters. He often said his lord rewarded the distant and punished kin without favor, that rank required merit and law spared no grandee—so good and simple men alike forgot themselves in his service.

sentences.zh: 」其明年，北詣亮諮事，送者數百，車乘盈路，裔還書與所親曰：「近者涉道，晝夜接客，不得寧息，人自敬丞相長史，男子張君嗣附之，疲倦欲死。

translations.literal: " The next year, going north to consult Liang on affairs, several hundred saw him off, carriages filled the road; Yi returned a letter to those close saying, "Lately traveling the road, day and night receiving guests, unable to obtain quiet rest—men themselves revere the chief clerk to the chancellor; the fellow Zhang Jinsi attached to it—weary nearly to death."
translations.idiomatic: The next year he rode north to see Zhuge Liang; hundreds saw him off and the road was jammed with carts. He wrote home that he had entertained callers day and night, that people honored the chief clerk’s office, and that poor Zhang Jinsi, hitched to that title, was exhausted unto death.

sentences.zh: 」其談啁流速，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His jesting banter was fluent and quick; all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His witty, rapid talk was always in this vein.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以为谈啁贵於机捷，书疏可容留意。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi thinks jesting banter values quick wit; letters and memorials may allow careful attention.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that banter prizes quick wit while letters allow deliberation.

sentences.zh: 今因书疏之巧，以著谈啁之速，非其理也。〉

translations.literal: Now relying on the skill of letters and memorials to display jesting banter's speed is not its principle.〉
translations.idiomatic: To infer his conversational speed from the polish of a written note is misleading.〉

sentences.zh: 少與犍為楊恭友善，恭早死，遺孤未數歲，裔迎留，與分屋而居，事恭母如母。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Yang Gong of Qianwei; Gong died early, leaving an orphan not several years old; Yi welcomed and kept him, dwelling in divided houses, serving Gong's mother as mother.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had befriended Yang Gong of Qianwei; when Gong died leaving a small child, Zhang Yi took the boy in, housed him separately, and honored Gong’s mother as his own.

sentences.zh: 恭之子息長大，為之娶婦，買田宅產業，使立門戶。

translations.literal: Gong's sons and heirs grew great; for them he took wives, bought fields, houses, and estates, causing them to establish households.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy grew up, Zhang Yi found him a wife, bought land and a house, and set him up with his own household.

sentences.zh: 撫恤故舊，振贍衰宗，行義甚至。

translations.literal: He comforted and pitied old associates, relieved and aided declining clans; conduct and righteousness reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He helped old friends and bolstered struggling kinsmen with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 加輔漢將軍，領長史如故。

translations.literal: He was added General Who Assists Han, leading chief clerk as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who assists Han while keeping the chief clerkship.

sentences.zh: 建興八年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 230.

sentences.zh: 子毣嗣，

translations.literal: The son Mao succeeded,
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Mao inherited the title,

sentences.zh: 〈毣音忙角反，见字林，曰“毣，思貌也”。〉

translations.literal: 〈Mao is read mang-jue fan, seen in the Zilin, stating "Mao, appearance of thought."〉
translations.idiomatic: The commentary gives Mao’s reading (mang-jue fan) and cites the Zilin gloss “thoughtful mien.”〉

sentences.zh: 歷三郡守、監軍。

translations.literal: He passed through three commandery governorships and army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of three commanderies and as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 毣郁，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Mao's son Yu was palace attendant to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao’s son Yu became a palace attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 楊洪字季休，犍為武陽人也。

translations.literal: Yang Hong, courtesy name Jixiu, was a man of Wuyang in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong, styled Jixiu, came from Wuyang in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時歷部諸郡。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he passed through service in the various commanderies of the department.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he served in several commanderies of the province.

sentences.zh: 先主定蜀，太守李嚴命為功曹。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu; Administrator Li Yan appointed him merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Bei took Shu, Governor Li Yan made him merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 嚴欲徒郡治捨，洪固諫不聽，遂辭功曹，請退。

translations.literal: Yan wished to move the commandery seat's lodging; Hong firmly remonstrated but was not listened to; thereupon he resigned merit clerk and requested withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan wanted to move the commandery seat; Yang Hong protested firmly and, ignored, resigned as merit clerk and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 嚴

translations.literal: Yan
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan

translations.literal: (wished)
translations.idiomatic: (wished)

sentences.zh: 薦洪於州，為

translations.literal: recommended Hong to the province, as
translations.idiomatic: recommended him to the province as

sentences.zh: （蜀部從事）

translations.literal: (Shu department aide)
translations.idiomatic: (Shu department aide)

sentences.zh: [部蜀從事]。

translations.literal: [department Shu aide].
translations.idiomatic: [department aide for Shu].

sentences.zh: 先主爭漢中，急書發兵，軍師將軍諸葛亮以問洪，洪曰：「漢中則益州咽喉，存亡之機會，若無漢中則無蜀矣，此家門之禍也。

translations.literal: The First Sovereign contested Hanzhong; urgent letters raised troops; Military Adviser General Zhuge Liang used this to ask Hong; Hong said, "Hanzhong is then Yizhou's throat; the pivot of survival or perishing; if there is no Hanzhong then there is no Shu—this is a calamity for the family gate."
translations.idiomatic: During the fight for Hanzhong, Zhuge Liang asked Yang Hong whether to send more troops. Hong replied that Hanzhong was Yizhou’s throat, that without it Shu could not stand, and that losing it would be a disaster for the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 方今之事，男子當戰，女子當運，發兵何疑？

translations.literal: As to the present matter, men ought to fight, women ought to transport—what doubt in raising troops?
translations.idiomatic: Men should fight and women haul supplies—there should be no hesitation in mobilizing.

sentences.zh: 」時蜀郡太守法正從先主北行，亮於是表洪領蜀郡太守，眾事皆辦，遂使即真。

translations.literal: " At the time Shu Commandery Administrator Fa Zheng followed the First Sovereign north; Liang thereupon memorialized Hong to lead Administrator of Shu commandery; all affairs were handled, then caused him to take full office.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Zheng had gone north with Liu Bei, so Zhuge Liang had Yang Hong appointed acting governor of Shu; he handled every task and was soon confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉為益州治中從事。

translations.literal: Shortly, he was transferred to Yizhou administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to administrative aide for Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，丞相亮北住漢中，欲用張裔為留府長史，問洪何如？

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chancellor Liang north lodged at Hanzhong, wished to use Zhang Yi as chief clerk of the rear headquarters, asked Hong how it was?
translations.idiomatic: In 227, with Zhuge Liang in Hanzhong, he considered making Zhang Yi chief clerk of the rear headquarters and asked Yang Hong’s opinion.

sentences.zh: 洪對曰：「裔天姿明察，長於治劇，才誠堪之，然性不公平，恐不可專任，不如留向朗。

translations.literal: Hong replied saying, "Yi's heaven-given nature is clear and perceptive; he excels at governing difficult matters; talent truly suffices for it, yet his nature is not fair and even; I fear he cannot be solely entrusted—better retain Xiang Lang."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong said Zhang Yi was sharp and excellent at knotty administration but partial by temperament and unsafe alone; Xiang Lang would be a steadier choice to stay behind.

sentences.zh: 朗情偽差少，裔隨從目下，效其器能，於事兩善。

translations.literal: Lang's feelings of falsehood are somewhat less; Yi following under the eye, displaying his tools and ability—on affairs both good.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Lang was the more even-tempered; Zhang Yi could still accompany the army and prove his talents—both uses would serve the state.

sentences.zh: 」初，裔少與洪親善。

translations.literal: " At first, in youth Yi and Hong were intimate and good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi and Yang Hong had been close since youth.

sentences.zh: 裔流放在吳，洪臨裔郡，裔子郁給郡吏，微過受罰，不特原假。

translations.literal: Yi was exiled in Wu; Hong came to Yi's commandery; Yi's son Yu supplied commandery clerks, slight fault received punishment, not especially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhang Yi was a hostage in Wu, Yang Hong governed his old commandery; Zhang Yi’s son Yu served there and was punished for a minor fault without special leniency.

sentences.zh: 裔後還聞之，深以為恨，與洪情好有損。

translations.literal: Yi later returned and heard of it, deeply took it as resentment; with Hong affection and friendship had damage.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yi returned and learned of it, he nursed a deep grudge and their friendship cooled.

sentences.zh: 及洪見亮出，至裔許，具說所言。

translations.literal: When Hong saw Liang go out, arrived at Yi's lodging, fully told what was said.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Hong’s interview with Zhuge Liang he went to Zhang Yi and repeated every word.

sentences.zh: 裔答洪曰：「公留我了矣，明府不能止。

translations.literal: Yi answered Hong saying, "The Duke has kept me indeed; the enlightened prefect could not stop it."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi told him the chancellor had already decided to keep him and no governor could change it.

sentences.zh: 」時人或疑洪意自欲作長史，或疑洪知裔自嫌，不願裔處要職，典後事也。

translations.literal: " At the time some suspected Hong's intention was himself to wish to become chief clerk, or suspected Hong knew Yi himself grudged, did not wish Yi to hold key office, directing rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Some thought Yang Hong wanted the chief clerk’s post for himself; others thought he knew Zhang Yi would refuse the rear post and spoke accordingly.

sentences.zh: 後裔與司鹽校尉岑述不和，至於忿恨。

translations.literal: Later Yi and Colonel Director of Salt Cen Shu were not harmonious, reaching to resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Yi quarreled bitterly with Cen Shu, the colonel director of salt.

sentences.zh: 亮與裔書曰：「君昔在[陌]下，營壞，吾之用心，食不知味；

translations.literal: Liang wrote Yi a letter saying, "Sir, formerly below the roads [at Deyang], the camp was ruined—my heart's use, eating did not know flavor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang wrote that when Zhang Yi’s camp was broken on the Deyang plain, he had been so anxious he could not taste his food;

sentences.zh: 後流洪迸南海，相為悲歎，寢不安席；

translations.literal: later when rumor had you cast into the South Sea, mutually for each other mourned and sighed, lying did not secure mat;
translations.idiomatic: when rumor said you had been banished to the southern seas, he had grieved with you and could not sleep at ease;

sentences.zh: 及其來還，委付大任，同獎王室，自以為與君古之石交也。

translations.literal: and when you came back, entrusted great charge, together aided the royal house—I thought myself with you ancient stone friendship.
translations.idiomatic: and after his return, when Zhuge Liang entrusted him with weighty office to help the house of Han, he had thought theirs the “stone friendship” of old.

sentences.zh: 石交之道，舉仇以相益，割骨肉以相明，猶不相謝也，況吾但委意於元儉，而君不能忍邪？

translations.literal: Stone friendship's way raises enemy to mutually benefit, cuts flesh and bone to mutually clarify, still does not decline—how much more I only entrusted intention to Yuanjian, yet you cannot endure?
translations.idiomatic: True friends recommend even a personal foe when it helps the state and cut kin ties to prove good faith—could Zhang Yi not bear Zhuge Liang’s leaning on Cen Shu (Yuanjian)?

sentences.zh: 」論者由是明洪無私。

translations.literal: " Discussers from this clarified Hong had no selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers then saw that Yang Hong had acted without private motive.

sentences.zh: 洪少不好學問，而忠清款亮，憂公如家，事繼母至孝。

translations.literal: Hong in youth did not love learning and inquiry, yet was loyal, pure, sincere, and bright, worried for the ducal as for family, served stepmother with utmost filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong had little scholarly bent but was loyal, candid, devoted to the public good as to his own kin, and deeply filial to his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 六年卒官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 228.

sentences.zh: 始洪為李嚴功曹，嚴未

translations.literal: At first Hong was Li Yan's merit clerk; Yan not yet
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hong had been merit clerk to Li Yan, before Yan

translations.literal: (arrived)
translations.idiomatic: (had yet reached)

sentences.zh: [去]犍為而洪已為蜀郡。

translations.literal: [gone] from Qianwei yet Hong was already Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: [left] Qianwei, Yang Hong was already governor of Shu.

sentences.zh: 洪迎門下書佐何祗，有才策功干，舉郡吏，數年為廣漢太守，時洪亦尚在蜀郡。

translations.literal: Hong welcomed gate clerk He Zhi, having talent, stratagem, merit, and capability; recommended commandery clerk; in several years became Administrator of Guanghan; at the time Hong also still was in Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong had promoted his clerk He Zhi, a man of talent, to county service; within a few years He became governor of Guanghan while Yang Hong still governed Shu.

sentences.zh: 是以西土鹹服諸葛亮能盡時人之器用也。

translations.literal: Therefore the western lands all submitted that Zhuge Liang could exhaust the tools and use of men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: People in the west marveled that Zhuge Liang could employ every man to the full measure of his gifts.

sentences.zh: 〈益部耆旧传杂记曰：每朝会，祗次洪坐。

translations.literal: 〈The Yibu qijiu zhuan miscellaneous record states: At each court assembly, Zhi ranked below Hong's seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Yibu qijiu zhuan notes that at court He Zhi always sat below Yang Hong.

sentences.zh: 嘲祗曰：“君马何驶？

translations.literal: He teased Zhi saying, "Sir, why do your horses gallop so fast?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hong teased him: "Why are your horses so fast?"

sentences.zh: ”祗曰：“故吏马不敢驶，但明府未著鞭耳。

translations.literal: " Zhi said, "Your former clerk's horses dare not gallop fast—only the enlightened prefect has not yet applied the whip."
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi replied that a former subordinate’s horses would not outrun his patron’s—unless the governor had not yet raised his whip.

sentences.zh: ”众传之以为笑。

translations.literal: " The crowd passed it on as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The story became a standing joke at court.

sentences.zh: 祗字君肃，少寒贫，为人宽厚通济，体甚壮大，又能饮食，好声色，不持节俭，故时人少贵之者。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Junsu, in youth was cold and poor; as a man he was generous, mild, and accommodating; his body was very large and strong, and again able to eat and drink; loved sounds and colors, did not maintain frugality; therefore men of the time few esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi, styled Junsu, grew up in poverty. He was generous and easygoing, built like a wrestler, with a huge appetite and a taste for music and women; because he lived loosely, contemporaries thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 尝梦井中生桑，以问占梦赵直，直曰：“桑非井中之物，会当移植；

translations.literal: He once dreamed mulberry grew in a well; he used this to ask dream-diviner Zhao Zhi; Zhi said, "Mulberry is not a thing in a well; in due course it will be transplanted;
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed of mulberry sprouting in a well and asked the diviner Zhao Zhi, who said mulberry did not belong in a well and foretold a transfer to another post;

sentences.zh: 然桑字四十下八，君寿恐不过此。

translations.literal: yet the graph sang (mulberry) decomposes as forty plus eight—your lifespan I fear will not pass this."
translations.idiomatic: yet the graph sang, meaning mulberry, is built from the pieces for forty and eight, so your years may not pass forty-eight."

sentences.zh: ”祗笑言“得此足矣”。

translations.literal: " Zhi laughed saying "Obtaining this suffices."
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi laughed and said that would be enough for him.

sentences.zh: 初仕郡，后为督军从事。

translations.literal: At first he served the commandery, later became aide on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the commandery office and rose to aide on army affairs.

sentences.zh: 时诸葛亮用法峻密，阴闻祗游戏放纵，不勤所职，尝奄往录狱。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuge Liang used law stern and tight; secretly heard Zhi played and was unrestrained, not diligent in his duty; once suddenly went to record the prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang’s justice was strict; hearing that He Zhi was carousing and neglecting duty, he once descended on the jail without warning to audit the dockets.

sentences.zh: 众人咸为祗惧。

translations.literal: The host all for Zhi feared.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone feared for him.

sentences.zh: 祗密闻之，夜张灯火见囚，读诸解状。

translations.literal: Zhi secretly heard it; at night spread lamps and fire, saw prisoners, read the various plea documents.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi got wind of the visit, lit the prison lamps that night, interviewed the inmates, and studied every plea.

sentences.zh: 诸葛晨往，祗悉已闇诵，答对解释，无所凝滞，亮甚异之。

translations.literal: Zhuge went in the morning; Zhi all had already recited by dark; answering and replying explaining, nothing stuck or halted; Liang greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang arrived at dawn, He Zhi had memorized the files and answered every question without hesitation, which greatly impressed the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 出补成都令，时郫县令缺，以祗兼二县。

translations.literal: Sent out to fill Chengdu magistrate; at the time Pi county magistrate was vacant; with Zhi concurrently holding two counties.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as magistrate of Chengdu and, with Pi county also vacant, was given both districts.

sentences.zh: 二县户口猥多，切近都治，饶诸奸秽，每比人，常眠睡，值其觉寤，辄得奸诈，众咸畏祗之发摘，或以为有术，无敢欺者。

translations.literal: The two counties' households and mouths were very many, cutting close to the metropolitan administration, abundant in various treachery and filth; each time comparing people, he constantly feigned sleep; when they awoke, then obtained treachery and fraud; all feared Zhi's exposing, some thought he had technique; none dared deceive.
translations.idiomatic: Both counties were populous, close to the capital, and rife with crime. At hearings He Zhi often seemed to doze; when suspects woke to his questions he caught their lies. People thought him uncanny and no one dared cheat him.

sentences.zh: 使人投算，祗听其读而心计之，不差升合，其精如此。

translations.literal: He had men cast counting rods; Zhi listened to their reading and reckoned in mind, not missing a sheng or he—his precision was thus.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks read tallies aloud, he computed in his head without missing a measure—such was his precision.

sentences.zh: 汶山夷不安，以祗为汶山太守，民夷服信。

translations.literal: Wenshan Yi were not peaceful; with Zhi as Wenshan Administrator, people and Yi submitted in trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenshan tribes grew restless, He Zhi was made their governor and won the trust of Chinese and tribesmen alike.

sentences.zh: 迁广汉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as governor of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 后夷反叛，辞“令得前何府君，乃能安我耳”！

translations.literal: Later the Yi rebelled, declaring "Only if we obtain the former He prefect can we be settled!"
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes rebelled again, they demanded the return of “our old Governor He” before they would submit.

sentences.zh: 时难屈祗，拔祗族人为，汶山复得安。

translations.literal: At the time it was hard to bend Zhi to return; they raised a man of Zhi's clan to [the post], and Wenshan again obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi could not be spared from his new post, so a kinsman of his clan was promoted in his stead and Wenshan grew calm again.

sentences.zh: 转祗为犍为。

translations.literal: Zhi was transferred to Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhi was then moved to Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 年四十八卒，如直所言。

translations.literal: At forty-eight sui he died, as Zhi had spoken.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight, exactly as Zhao Zhi had predicted.

sentences.zh: 后有广汉王离，字伯元，亦以才幹显。

translations.literal: Later there was Wang Li of Guanghan, courtesy name Boyuan, who also by talent and capacity was illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Li of Guanghan, styled Boyuan, also rose on ability and administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 为督军从事，推法平当，稍迁，代祗为犍为太守，治有美绩，虽聪明不及祗，而文采过之也。〉

translations.literal: He became aide on military affairs, pushed law even and fitting, gradually was promoted, replaced Zhi as Administrator of Qianwei, governance had fine achievements; although cleverness did not reach Zhi, yet literary polish surpassed him.〉
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide on army affairs, applied the law evenhandedly, rose step by step, succeeded He Zhi as governor of Qianwei, and governed well—less brilliant than He Zhi but the finer writer.〉

sentences.zh: 費詩字公舉，犍為南安人也。

translations.literal: Fei Shi, courtesy name Gongju, was a man of Nan'an in Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Shi, styled Gongju, came from Nan'an in Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 劉璋時為綿竹令，先主攻綿竹時，詩先舉城降。

translations.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was Mianzhu magistrate; when the First Sovereign attacked Mianzhu, Shi first raised the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Zhang he was magistrate of Mianzhu and was the first to surrender the town when Liu Bei attacked.

sentences.zh: 成都既定，先主領益州牧，以詩為督軍從事，出為牂牁太守，還為州前部司馬。

translations.literal: When Chengdu was already settled, the First Sovereign led Governor of Yizhou, appointing Shi aide on military affairs, sent out as Administrator of Zangke, returned as forward-division major of the province.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell, Liu Bei as governor of Yizhou made him an army aide, then governor of Zangke, then brought him back as forward-division major of the province.

sentences.zh: 先主為漢中王，遣詩拜關羽為前將軍，羽聞黃忠為後將軍，

translations.literal: The First Sovereign became King of Hanzhong, sent Shi to invest Guan Yu as General of the Van; Yu heard Huang Zhong was General of the Rear,
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong, he sent Fei Shi to present Guan Yu with appointment as general of the van. Guan Yu learned that Huang Zhong had been named general of the rear,

translations.literal: (Yu)
translations.idiomatic: (Guan Yu)

sentences.zh: 怒曰：「大丈夫終不與老兵同列！

translations.literal: angrily said, "A great man in the end will not share rank with an old soldier!"
translations.idiomatic: and fumed that a gentleman could not stand in the same row as an old soldier.

sentences.zh: 」不肯受拜。

translations.literal: " He refused to accept the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the commission.

sentences.zh: 詩謂羽曰：「夫立王業者，所用非一。

translations.literal: Shi said to Yu, "Now he who establishes kingly enterprise employs not one kind."
translations.idiomatic: Fei Shi told him that founding a royal enterprise required many kinds of men.

sentences.zh: 昔蕭、曹與高祖少小親舊，而陳、韓亡命後主，論其班列，韓最居上，未聞蕭、曹以此為怨。

translations.literal: Formerly Xiao and Cao with the Supreme Ancestor from youth were intimate old friends, yet Chen and Han were fugitives who came later as lords; discussing their order of ranks, Han was highest; I have not heard Xiao and Cao on this account harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He and Cao Shen had grown up with Gaozu, while Chen Ping and Han Xin arrived as fugitives, yet Han Xin ranked above them in court order without rousing Xiao’s or Cao’s resentment.

sentences.zh: 今

translations.literal: Now
translations.idiomatic: Today

sentences.zh: （漢王）

translations.literal: (King of Han)
translations.idiomatic: (the king of Han)

sentences.zh: [漢中王]以一時之功隆崇於漢升，然意之輕重，寧當與君侯齊乎！

translations.literal: [King of Hanzhong] by a moment's merit exalts Hansheng, yet as to the weight of favor, how could it be equal to you, lord!
translations.idiomatic: the king of Hanzhong has honored Hansheng for one exploit, but His Majesty’s regard for you, my lord, surely still outweighs that.

sentences.zh: 且王與君侯臂猶一體，同休等戚，禍福共之，愚為君侯不宜計官號之高下、爵祿之多少為意也。

translations.literal: Moreover the king and you, lord, are arms as one body, share rest and equal sorrow, fortune and misfortune together; your foolish servant thinks you, lord, ought not take to heart the height or lowness of office titles, the much or little of noble rank and stipend.
translations.idiomatic: You and the king are as two arms on one body, sharing weal and woe; you should not fuss over title or pay.

sentences.zh: 僕一介之使，銜命之人，君侯不受拜，如是便還，但相為惜此舉動，恐有後悔耳！

translations.literal: Your servant, a single messenger, a man bearing mandate—if you, lord, do not accept investiture, thus I will return, only mutually for you pity this movement, fearing there will be later regret!
translations.idiomatic: I am only an envoy; if you refuse the seal I must go back empty-handed, and I fear you may regret such a gesture.

sentences.zh: 」羽大感悟，遂即受拜。

translations.literal: " Yu greatly was moved and awakened, thereupon at once accepted investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu was deeply moved and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 後群臣議欲推漢中王稱尊號，詩上疏曰：「殿下以曹操父子逼主篡位，故乃羈旅萬里，糾合士眾，將以討賊。

translations.literal: Later the host of ministers deliberated wishing to urge the King of Hanzhong to assume the exalted title; Shi submitted a memorial saying, "Your Highness because Cao Cao and his son forced the ruler and usurped the throne, therefore then wandered in travel ten thousand li, gathered and united gentlemen and hosts, about to use them to strike the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: When the court urged the king of Hanzhong to take the imperial title, Fei Shi memorialized that Liu Bei had crossed a thousand leagues and raised an army to punish Cao Cao’s usurpation.

sentences.zh: 今天敵未克，而先主自立，恐人心疑惑。

translations.literal: Now heaven's foe is not yet overcome, yet the First Sovereign establishes himself—I fear people's hearts will be doubtful and confused.
translations.idiomatic: The great enemy was still unbeaten, he warned, and proclaiming oneself emperor now would only unsettle popular feeling.

sentences.zh: 昔高祖與楚約，先破秦者王。

translations.literal: Formerly the Supreme Ancestor made covenant with Chu: whoever first broke Qin would be king.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had sworn with Chu that whoever first destroyed Qin would be king.

sentences.zh: 及屠咸陽，獲子嬰，猶懷推讓，況今殿下未出門庭，便欲自立邪！

translations.literal: When he slaughtered Xianyang, captured Ziying, still cherished yielding and declining—how much more now Your Highness has not yet gone out the gate and courtyard, then wishes to establish yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Even after taking Xianyang and capturing Ying Ziying, Gaozu had hesitated to claim the throne; how could Liu Bei, who had not yet left his own threshold, rush to declare himself?

sentences.zh: 愚臣誠不為殿下取也。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant truly does not approve for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot approve this course for Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 」由是忤指，左遷部永昌從事。

translations.literal: " From this he offended intent, was demoted left to department Yongchang aide.
translations.idiomatic: For this bluntness he was demoted to an aide in Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 〈习凿齿曰：夫创本之君，须大定而后正己，纂统之主，俟速建以系众心，是故惠公朝虏而子圉夕立，更始尚存而光武举号，夫岂忘主徼利，社稷之故也。

translations.literal: 〈Xi Zuochi states: Now the lord who founds the root must await great settling then rectify himself; the lord who continues the line waits on swift establishment to bind the multitude's hearts—therefore Duke Hui was captive at dawn and Ziyu was established at evening; Gengshi still existed yet Guangwu raised title—how could they forget the ruler and seek profit? It was for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi observes that a founder waits until the realm is settled before taking supreme rank, while a successor must act quickly to steady hearts—hence Duke Hui of Jin was captured in the morning and his heir enthroned that evening, and Guangwu took title while Gengshi still lived; such steps served the state, not private ambition.

sentences.zh: 今先主纠合义兵，将以讨贼。

translations.literal: Now the First Sovereign gathers righteous troops, about to use them to strike the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei had rallied a loyal host to punish the usurper.

sentences.zh: 贼强祸大，主没国丧，二祖之庙，绝而不祀，苟非亲贤，孰能绍此？

translations.literal: The rebels are strong, calamity great; the ruler perished, state mourned; the two ancestors' temples are cut off and not sacrificed—if not kin and worthy, who can continue this?
translations.idiomatic: The foe was powerful, the sovereign dead, the altars of the two Han founders untended—who but a worthy kinsman could renew the line?

sentences.zh: 嗣祖配天，非咸阳之譬，杖正讨逆，何推让之有？

translations.literal: Heir connects ancestor matching heaven—this is not Xianyang's comparison; leaning on rectitude to strike rebellion—what yielding and declining is there?
translations.idiomatic: To succeed the ancestors and match heaven is not the same as Gaozu’s moment at Xianyang; when one wields justice against traitors, there is no room for false modesty.

sentences.zh: 於此时也，不知速尊有德以奉大统，使民欣反正，世睹旧物，杖顺者齐心，附逆者同惧，可谓闇惑矣。

translations.literal: At this time, not knowing to speedily honor the virtuous to serve the great line, causing the people gladly to return to rectification, the age to behold old things, those leaning on compliance to unite hearts, those attaching to rebellion together to fear—may be called benighted and deluded.
translations.idiomatic: To delay enthroning a worthy heir at such a hour, letting the people rejoice in restoration and the wicked tremble, would be folly indeed.

sentences.zh: 其黜降也宜哉！

translations.literal: His demotion was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder Fei Shi was demoted!

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为凿齿论议，惟此论最善。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks in Zuochi's discussions and debates, only this discussion is best.〉
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi calls this the finest of Xi Zuochi’s arguments.〉

sentences.zh: 建興三年，隨諸葛亮南行，歸至漢陽縣，降人李鴻來詣亮，亮見鴻，時蔣琬與詩在坐。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianxing, he followed Zhuge Liang south; returning reached Hanyang county; surrendered man Li Hong came to visit Liang; Liang saw Hong; at the time Jiang Wan and Shi were seated.
translations.idiomatic: In 225, returning with Zhuge Liang from the southern campaign, they reached Hanyang county, where the defector Li Hong came to see Zhuge Liang; Jiang Wan and Fei Shi were present.

sentences.zh: 鴻曰：「聞過孟達許，適見王沖從南來，言往者達之去就，明公切齒，欲誅達妻子，賴先主不聽言。

translations.literal: Hong said, "I heard passing Meng Da's place, just then saw Wang Chong coming from the south, speaking of former times Da's going and coming, the enlightened lord gnashed teeth, wished to execute Da's wife and children, relied on the First Sovereign not listening to the words."
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong said he had stopped at Meng Da’s camp and met Wang Chong from the south, who told him Zhuge Liang had once been furious enough to execute Meng Da’s family until Liu Bei forbade it.

sentences.zh: 達曰：『諸葛亮見顧有本末，終不爾也。

translations.literal: Da said, 'Zhuge Liang's regard has beginning and end; in the end will not be thus.'
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da had replied that Zhuge Liang’s goodwill had always been consistent and he would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 』盡不信沖言，委仰明公，無復已已。

translations.literal: ' He wholly did not believe Chong's words, entrusted and looked up to the enlightened lord, no more end.
translations.idiomatic: He had refused to trust Wang Chong and placed his faith entirely in Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 」亮謂琬、詩曰：「還都當有書與子度相聞。

translations.literal: " Liang said to Wan and Shi, "When returning to the capital there ought to be a letter to exchange news with Zidu."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang told Jiang Wan and Fei Shi that back in the capital he would write to Meng Da.

sentences.zh: 」詩進曰：「孟達小子，昔事振威不忠，後又背叛先主，反覆之人，何足與書邪！

translations.literal: " Shi advanced saying, "Meng Da the petty fellow, formerly served General Who Strikes Terror disloyally, afterward again betrayed the First Sovereign—a man of back and forth—what worth to exchange letters!"
translations.idiomatic: Fei Shi objected that Meng Da had betrayed Liu Zhang and Liu Bei and was not worth a letter.

sentences.zh: 」亮默然不答。

translations.literal: " Liang was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang said nothing.

sentences.zh: 亮欲誘達以為外援，竟與達書曰：「往年南征，歲

translations.literal: Liang wished to entice Da to be an external aid; in the end wrote Da a letter saying, "In former years on the southern campaign, before the year
translations.idiomatic: To draw Meng Da as an ally in Wei, Zhuge Liang finally wrote: on the southern expedition of recent years, before that year

sentences.zh: （未及）

translations.literal: (not yet reached)
translations.idiomatic: (before the year had ended)

sentences.zh: [末及]還，適與李鴻會於漢陽，承知消息，慨然永歎，以存足下平素之志，豈徒空托名榮，貴為乘離乎！

translations.literal: had ended I returned, just then met Li Hong at Hanyang, received and knew your message, sighed long with feeling—thereby to preserve your foot's constant purpose—how merely empty entrusting name and glory, prized as riding estrangement!
translations.idiomatic: had closed I was still on the road; I met Li Hong at Hanyang and learned your mind. I sighed long for the loyalty you have always shown—surely you do not seek empty glory while we remain apart!

sentences.zh: 嗚呼孟子，斯實劉封侵陵足下，以傷先主待士之義。

translations.literal: Alas, Mengzi, this truly was Liu Feng encroaching and bullying you, thereby harming the First Sovereign's righteousness in treating gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Meng Da—it was Liu Feng’s bullying that wronged you and violated the late emperor’s duty to his men.

sentences.zh: 又鴻道王沖造作虛語，云足下量度吾心，不受沖說。

translations.literal: Again Hong related that Wang Chong fabricated empty words, saying you measured my mind and did not accept Chong's tale.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong also said Wang Chong’s story was invented, and he praised you for seeing my true intent and rejecting the lie.

sentences.zh: 尋表明之言，追平生之好，依依東望，故遣有書。

translations.literal: Clarifying what was declared above, pursuing the friendship of a lifetime, lingering as I gaze east—I therefore send this letter.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing in mind what was said above and our old friendship, I gaze east and send this letter.

sentences.zh: 」達得亮書，數相交通，辭欲叛魏。

translations.literal: " When Da obtained Liang's letter, repeatedly exchanged communication, declared intent wishing to rebel against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Da answered repeatedly and began plotting to revolt from Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏遣司馬宣王征之，即斬滅達。

translations.literal: Wei sent Sima the King of Xuan to campaign against him; at once beheaded and destroyed Da.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Sima Yi against him and had him killed at once.

sentences.zh: 亮亦以達無款誠之心，故不救助也。

translations.literal: Liang also because Da had no sincere and honest heart, therefore did not rescue and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang did not send help because he judged Meng Da insincere.

sentences.zh: 蔣琬秉政，以詩為諫議大夫，卒於家。

translations.literal: Jiang Wan held government, appointed Shi grandee remonstrant; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiang Wan’s regency Fei Shi became grandee remonstrant and died at home.

sentences.zh: 王沖者，廣漢人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chong was a man of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong was from Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 為牙門將，統屬江州李嚴。

translations.literal: He was camp-gate general, commanded under Jiangzhou Li Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was a camp-gate general under Li Yan of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 為嚴所疾，懼罪降魏。

translations.literal: Yan was jealous of him; fearing punishment he surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan disliked him, so fearing punishment he defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以沖為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Chong Administrator of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made him governor of Leling.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛蜀世谱曰：诗子立，晋散骑常侍。

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng's Shu shìpu states: Shi's son Li, Jin gentleman attendant at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng’s Shu genealogy records Fei Shi’s son Li as a Jin gentleman attendant at leisure.

sentences.zh: 自后益州诸费有名位者，多是诗之后也。〉

translations.literal: From afterward Yizhou's various Fei who had fame and position were mostly Shi's posterity.〉
translations.idiomatic: Most later Fei clansmen of note in Yizhou descended from him.〉

sentences.zh: 评曰：霍峻孤城不倾，王连固节不移，向朗好学不倦，张裔肤敏应机，杨洪乃心忠公，费诗率意而言，皆有可纪焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Huo Jun's lone city did not topple; Wang Lian's firm integrity did not shift; Xiang Lang loved learning without weariness; Zhang Yi was perceptive and keen, responding to opportunity; Yang Hong's heart was loyal to the ducal; Fei Shi spoke following his mind—all had what is worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: The historian’s judgment: Huo Jun held a lone city; Wang Lian kept faith; Xiang Lang never tired of study; Zhang Yi was quick and resourceful; Yang Hong was utterly loyal; Fei Shi spoke his mind—all merit remembrance.

sentences.zh: 以先主之广济，诸葛之准绳，诗吐直言，犹用陵迟，况庸后乎哉！

translations.literal: Given the First Sovereign's broad succor, Zhuge's marking cord—Shi spat forth straight words, still was used declining—how much more vulgar successors!
translations.idiomatic: Yet even Liu Bei’s generosity and Zhuge Liang’s fairness could not save Fei Shi from demotion for blunt speech—what hope for lesser lords thereafter?
